backing.backing_score_basis: ⚠️⚠️ NOT AN INHERITANCE FROM usdai 7.0, BECAUSE sUSDai HOLDS A DIFFERENT ASSET SET FROM ITS PARENT. usdai's reserve is PYUSD at par; sUSDai holds a USDai idle buffer PLUS a GPU/equipment loan book originated through MetaStreet. Under the spec's 2026-09-11 discriminator a wrapper holding something its underlying does not is scored ON MERITS, not set equal. ✅ THE OVERCOLLATERALIZATION IS REAL AND STRUCTURED: 70-80% LTV, a ~10% DSRA, and sCHIP beneath it — a genuine three-layer cushion. ⚠️ BUT THE COLLATERAL DEPRECIATES, WHICH IS UNUSUAL IN THIS CORPUS: GPU and AI hardware loses value on a TECHNOLOGY curve rather than a credit curve, so an LTV struck today is not the LTV at default. ⚠️ AND MOST CAPITAL IS NOW DEPLOYED: loansReserves $104M -> $257.3M against totalAssets $354.99M, so the idle buffer is proportionally thinner than in May. ⚠️⚠️ THE DECISIVE DOCK IS THE DUAL MARK — THE VALUE SHOWN IS NOT THE VALUE YOU EXIT AT. depositSharePrice() returns 1.104646 and is quoted as NAV; redemptions settle on a conservative 1.0998, and totalAssets() is struck on the OPTIMISTIC basis too. So headline AUM and headline NAV are both optimistic while exits are not — a ~44bp gap that is STRUCTURAL, not an error. Model exits against 1.0998.

backing.backing_score_denominator: ⚠️ DO NOT COMPUTE NAV AS totalAssets/totalSupply — for sUSDai it returns $1.745 and is WRONG. The correct getter is convertToAssets(ONE_SHARE). ⚠️⚠️ AND ONE_SHARE IS NOT ALWAYS 1e18 — STATE THE DECIMALS OR THE CORRECTION PROPAGATES A SECOND ERROR. sUSDai is verified 18-decimal (2026-09-12, Arbitrum, 0x0B2b2B2076d95dda7817e785989fE353fe955ef9), so 1e18 is correct HERE. On a 6-decimal share one share is 1e6, and convertToAssets(1e18) returns a number ~1e12 too large that is not a price at all. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO THAT THE TWO METHODS DIVERGE ONLY ON SOME VAULTS: for a plain ERC-4626 they agree (tidresearch checked hastra-prime — totalAssets/totalSupply 1.058797 vs convertToAssets(1e6) 1.058803, agreeing to six places). sUSDai is ERC-7540 ASYNC, which is why they diverge here. So the rule is not 'never divide' — it is 'divide only after confirming the vault is synchronous, and use the share's own decimals'. ⚠️ The feed carries no collateral_ratio for this asset, so the authored 5.0 has nothing beside it to agree or disagree with.

dependencies.underlying_score_basis: MEASURES THE COUNTERPARTY SET. ⚠️ BELOW usdai's 5.5, AND THE WRAPPER EQUAL-RULE DOES NOT BIND — sUSDai holds a different asset set, so the spec's discriminator puts it outside the rule. It inherits every counterparty usdai has and adds its own: (1) the whole of usdai's set arrives UNDILUTED — PYUSD, therefore Paxos, therefore PYUSD's reserve banks; (2) METASTREET as originator and servicer of the loan book, a role with NO SUBSTITUTE — if it stops servicing, the loans do not re-home; (3) the BORROWER SET in the GPU/equipment book, whose concentration the Volatility row flags; (4) Permian Labs as operator; (5) four chains — arb, plasma, eth, base. ⚠️⚠️ AND ONE DEPENDENCY THAT RUNS BACKWARDS: sUSDai IS 99.3% OF FLUID'S GHO MARKET ON PLASMA. $8,644,704 posted against $7,411,720 borrowed, 4.26pp of headroom, and a 4.74% mark drop takes that book to its liquidation threshold. That is Fluid depending on sUSDai, not the reverse — BUT THE CHANNEL CLOSES THE LOOP: a liquidation there is forced selling of sUSDai into sUSDai's OWN secondary, moving the mark that triggered it. REFLEXIVITY, NOT COUNTERPARTY EXPOSURE, so it is not priced as reliance — it is recorded because a holder reading only the counterparty list would never see it.
